title: Tactics level-up
blurb: Two ideas win a lot of games: take away the piece that is doing the defending, and look for an in-between move before you recapture. Then learn to use sacrifices and to calculate to the end.
deeperTitle: Deflection, attraction, sacrifices; calculating several moves

core.title: Two ways to win material
body: Many tactics use the same two ideas. **Remove the defender**: a piece protected only once falls when you take or chase its protector.
And the **in-between move**: when your opponent captures, do not recapture on autopilot. Look for something stronger first.

core.title: Remove the defender
body: A piece that is protected only once is only as safe as its protector. Here the rook attacks the bishop on c5, and the knight on a6 is its **only** defender.
Take the defender, and the bishop is yours.

board.caption: The bishop on c5 is attacked once and defended once, by the knight on a6.

core.prompt: Tap the piece that defends the black bishop on c5.
core.explain: The knight on **a6** is the only defender. That makes it the target.

core.prompt: Win the bishop on c5 by removing its defender.
core.hint: Which of your pieces can take the knight on a6?
core.explain: **Bxa6** takes the defender. If Black recaptures on a6, **Rxc5** wins the bishop. Either way you come out a piece ahead.

core.prompt: The bishop on d5 is attacked by your queen. What is holding it up? Remove it.
core.hint: Look at what defends the bishop on d5.
core.explain: The knight on f4 is the bishop’s only defender. **Nxf4** takes it, and the bishop on d5 falls next.

core.title: The in-between move
body: Your opponent captures one of your pieces. The obvious reply is to take back. But first ask: **is there a check, a bigger capture or a threat I can play right now?**
The in-between move (**zwischenzug**) comes first, and the recapture can wait.

core.prompt: Black’s bishop has just taken your bishop on d3. Do not take back. Find the better move.
core.hint: What does your knight attack? Something worth more than a bishop.
core.explain: **Nxc5** takes the rook first. If you recapture with **cxd3**, the c-file opens and Black plays **…Rc1#**.

core.prompt: Black’s bishop has just taken on g3. Do not recapture. You can end the game.
core.hint: Black’s king has no escape squares. Which rook can check on the back rank?
core.explain: **Re8#**. The pawns on f7, g7 and h7 box the king in, and nothing can take the rook. Always look for a check before you recapture.

core.title: Remove the defender
core.intro: Find the defender, and take it away. White and Black.

puzzles.hint: The knight on b5 is protected by the bishop on c6.
puzzles.explain: The bishop on c6 protects the knight on b5 **and** the back rank. **Nxc6** takes it. If Black recaptures with the b-pawn, **Re8#** is checkmate; otherwise you stay a piece ahead.

puzzles.hint: What is holding up the knight on e5? And can the g7 pawn take back?
puzzles.explain: The bishop on f6 defends the knight. **Rxf6** takes it, and the pawn on g7 cannot take back because your queen pins it to the king. You win a piece and the knight on e5 is still attacked.

puzzles.hint: You are Black now. Which piece defends the bishop that your rook attacks?
puzzles.explain: The same idea from Black’s side: take the only defender, and the bishop falls.

core.title: In-between moves
core.intro: Black has just captured. Do not take back until you have looked for something stronger.

puzzles.hint: Your bishop attacks something bigger than the bishop that just took.
puzzles.explain: **Bxd6** takes the rook first. The automatic recapture on b3 would lose the game.

puzzles.hint: Your queen and the black queen are facing each other.
puzzles.explain: **Qxb7** takes the queen before anything else. The recapture on d4 can wait.

puzzles.hint: A check that also takes something.
puzzles.explain: **Nxh6+** takes a rook with check. The automatic recapture on b6 would lose.

deeper.title: Deflection and attraction
body: **Deflection** pulls a defender away from its job. **Attraction** (a decoy) lures a piece, often the king, onto a bad square.
Both usually start with a sacrifice, and they only work if the forcing line ends in checkmate or in winning more than you gave.

deeper.prompt: Black’s queen guards the back rank. Lure her away and finish the game: checkmate in two.
deeper.hint: Give up your queen with check, so that their queen has to take on c8.
deeper.explain: **Qc8+** attracts the queen to c8, and the rook takes it with checkmate: **Rxc8#**. Your queen was attacked by the rook on b6, but a check comes first.

deeper.prompt: Checkmate in three. Give up your queen, then a rook will finish. Which queen move starts it?
deeper.hint: The rook on d8 guards the back rank. How can you force it away?
deeper.explain: **Qxf7+** (protected by the rook on f4) drives the king to h8. **Qf8+** deflects the rook from d8, and **Rxf8#** is checkmate.

deeper.prompt: When is a sacrifice a good idea?
options: When the forcing line ends in checkmate, or wins more than it cost
deeper.explain: A sacrifice is a calculation, not a gamble. Follow every check, capture and threat to the end. If you cannot see the end, do not sacrifice.

deeper.title: Calculating several moves
body: List your **candidate moves**: checks first, then captures, then threats. For each one, follow the forcing replies to the end of the line.
If a line ends in mate or in a clear win, play it. If you cannot see the end, choose a safer move.

deeper.prompt: Checkmate in two. Your rook can capture with check. Find the capture.
deeper.hint: Check first. Their queen will have to block on d8.
deeper.explain: **Rxc8+** is check, and the only way to stop it is **…Qd8**, which blocks on d8 and is taken with checkmate: **Rxd8#**. You calculated every defence: there was only one.

deeper.title: Sacrifices and decoys
deeper.intro: You are Black in all three, so the board is flipped. Lure the piece away, then mate.

puzzles.hint: Give up your queen with check, so that their queen has to take.
puzzles.explain: The queen sacrifice **attracts** their queen to the back rank, and the rook mates.

puzzles.hint: The rook guards the back rank. Force it away.
puzzles.explain: The queen sacrifice drives the king into the corner, then deflects the rook from the back rank.

puzzles.hint: Check with a capture. Their queen must block.
puzzles.explain: Their queen is forced to block on the back rank, and the rook takes it with mate.

deeper.title: Checks first
deeper.intro: List your checks, then pick the one that leaves Black the fewest replies. Each of these is checkmate in two.

puzzles.hint: A queen check on the back rank. Where can Black block?
puzzles.explain: **Qa8+** forces the bishop to block on e8, and **Qxe8#** takes it with checkmate.

puzzles.hint: Take with check. Where does the king have to go?
puzzles.explain: **Qxf7+** drives the king to h8. Then **Qxg7#** is checkmate, because the bishop on c3 protects the queen.

puzzles.hint: You are Black. Check on the back rank, and see what the knight must do.
puzzles.explain: **Qd1+** forces the knight to block on e1, and **Qxe1#** is checkmate.

deeper.prompt: In what order should you look at candidate moves?
options: Checks first, then captures, then threats
Quiet moves first, forcing moves last
deeper.explain: Forcing moves leave your opponent the fewest replies, so you can calculate them to the end. That is the checklist from Day 6.
